messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 2-iodopyridine with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:
ligand:
L1: tBuBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

picks.reason: The proven L2/B3 pair makes the 4-carboxylate a useful positional-isomer test against the strong 5-carboxylate A13.
This heteroaryl-substituted 3-carboxylate tests whether the strong A13 motif tolerates a 5-heteroaryl group.
The thiophene analogue of A21 tests a related heteroaryl substituent while retaining the 3-carboxylate motif.
The simple 3-methylisoxazole tests whether A13's methylated ring contributes without its ester group.
The 5-methyl regioisomer of A15 probes whether methyl placement affects the additive response.
This 3-methyl-5-phenyl analogue tests whether a 5-aryl substituent can improve the 3-methylisoxazole scaffold.
The dimethyl analogue tests whether adding a second methyl group benefits the already favorable L2/B3 conditions.
The difluorophenyl analogue tests an electron-poor aryl substituent with the best-performing ligand and base.
The pyrrolyl-substituted 5-methylisoxazole explores whether a donor-rich heteroaryl substituent is beneficial.
The 5-phenylisoxazole tests a simple aryl substituent and its ring-position effect under the best conditions.
The 4-phenylisoxazole provides a positional-isomer comparison to the other phenylisoxazole additives.
The 3-phenylisoxazole completes the phenylisoxazole positional-isomer screen with the leading catalyst system.
The dibenzylamino-substituted 5-isomer tests whether a strongly donating substituent can enhance the additive effect.
This 3-isomer comparison tests whether the dibenzylamino additive's position changes performance.
The fused benzisoxazole tests whether a rigid, fused analogue can retain the benefit observed for A13.
The alternative benzisoxazole connectivity tests the effect of changing the fused heterocycle's atom arrangement.
A9 gave high yield with L2/B3, so testing it with L1 checks whether that additive response generalizes across the leading ligands.
This tests whether the strong A9/B3 combination transfers to L4, which also performed well with A13.
A17 was promising with L2/B3, and this run tests its compatibility with the other high-performing BrettPhos ligand.
B1 was weaker than B3 with A13, but testing it with the strong A9 additive checks for a useful base-additive interaction.
